title: Local finite freeness of the canonical truncation in degree zero
statement: Let T be a scheme, U an open subscheme, d a natural number, C a flat complex strictly supported in [0,d], Q a complex of finite-free modules strictly bounded above by d, and e : Q → C a quasi-isomorphism. For each t ∈ U, there is an open neighbourhood V ≤ U and a natural rank r such that degree zero of the canonical quotient truncation at zero of the restriction of Q to V is isomorphic to the rank-r free structure-sheaf module. The complex is fixed by Mathlib truncGE, not quantified as an arbitrary P.

source.place: Tags 0653 and 00NX; degree-zero cokernel in the local finite-free replacement

proof.text: Conjugate Q.d(-1,0) by the two supplied finite free isomorphisms. The cokernel universal property gives an explicit finite global presentation of Q.opcycles(0), via SheafOfModules.presentationOfIsCokernelFree. Its finite index types give finite presentation and therefore quasi-coherence. This is the proved private helper finitePresentation_opcycles_zero.

Apply the flatness substep to get IsFlatOver for Q.opcycles(0). Evaluate this hypothesis on two equal affine opens and normalize the identity ring map. The existing finitePresentation_sections_of_isFinitePresentation theorem gives finitely presented affine sections; the affine criterion isFiniteLocallyFree_of_isAffineOpen now gives finite local freeness. This is the proved private helper finiteLocallyFree_of_flat_finitePresentation.

Use exists_restrict_iso_free_of_isFiniteLocallyFree to obtain a neighbourhood W of the point in U.toScheme and a finite basis type. Send W into T by U.ι and use isoImage_ι_inv_ι to factor T.homOfLE through W. Pull back the trivialization through that isomorphism and identify the finite basis type with ULift(Fin(card)). This gives the finite free isomorphism for the pullback of the actual opcycles.

For the restricted complex QV, CochainComplex.truncGEXIsoOpcycles identifies degree zero of truncGE with QV.opcycles(0). Both opcycles objects are the cokernels of the respective degree (-1,0) differentials. Unique-up-to-isomorphism of cokernels and PreservesCokernel.iso for pullback give QV.opcycles(0) isomorphic to the pullback of Q.opcycles(0). Compose these explicit isomorphisms with the finite free trivialization. Pullback is a left adjoint, so this uses only preservation of cokernels, not exactness of open restriction.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_local_finiteFree_truncation_zero {T : Scheme.{u}} (U : T.Opens)
    (C Q : CochainComplex U.toScheme.Modules ℤ) (d : ℕ)
    (hCge : C.IsStrictlyGE 0) (hCle : C.IsStrictlyLE d)
    (hCflat : ∀ n : ℤ, (C.X n).IsFlatOver (𝟙 U.toScheme))
    (hQle : Q.IsStrictlyLE d)
    (hQfree : ∀ n : ℤ, ∃ r : ℕ,
      Nonempty (Q.X n ≅ SheafOfModules.free
        (R := U.toScheme.ringCatSheaf) (ULift.{u} (Fin r))))
    (e : Q ⟶ C) (he : QuasiIso e) (t : T) (ht : t ∈ U) :
    ∃ (V : T.Opens) (hVU : V ≤ U), t ∈ V ∧ ∃ r : ℕ,
      Nonempty ((CochainComplex.truncGE
        (((Modules.pullback (T.homOfLE hVU)).mapHomologicalComplex _).obj Q) 0).X 0 ≅
          SheafOfModules.free
          (R := V.toScheme.ringCatSheaf) (ULift.{u} (Fin r)))
